gemma4_verdict: Gemma 4 31B-it (dense, served via vLLM bitsandbytes int4 per Labmate's stack; community GGUF Q4_K_M ~20GB) is a strong academic-writing candidate but lacks any published academic-writing-specific evaluation. No WritingBench or EssayBench score has been released for any Gemma 4 variant as of June 2026. Its case rests on three pillars: (1) Strong reasoning/knowledge benchmarks that underpin argument quality and factual grounding — the closely-related 26B A4B sibling posts MMLU Pro 82.6% and GPQA Diamond 82.3% on the official Google/HuggingFace release, and the 31B dense is positioned as the strongest of the family (ranked #3 among open models on LMArena text). (2) Native document understanding: Gemma 4 includes Document/PDF parsing, chart comprehension, OCR (multilingual), and image input on all sizes, making it uniquely able to READ academic papers WITH their figures, tables, and equations rendered as images — a decisive advantage for paper critique where methodological weaknesses often live in figures/tables. (3) Built directly from Gemini 3 research, which historically produces fluent, well-structured long-form prose. Weaknesses: no community track record yet for academic prose, hedging calibration, or citation-format fidelity (BibTeX/natbib); LaTeX equation/table generation accuracy is unverified for Gemma 4 specifically (Gemma 3 27B was decent but not class-leading at LaTeX). The aggressive benchmark numbers circulating on SEO blogs (AIME 89.2%, LiveCodeBench 80%) should be treated cautiously; only the official-blog/HF 26B A4B figures are trustworthy. [uncertain on academic-prose quality, citation formatting, LaTeX accuracy]
qwen3_verdict: Qwen/Qwen3-32B has the strongest published evidence for academic writing of the two. On WritingBench (X-PLUG, arXiv 2503.05244) — whose six domains explicitly include 'Academic & Engineering' — Qwen3-32B-Instruct scores 8.64/10, essentially matching DeepSeek-R1 (8.55) and far above the Qwen3-32B-Base (6.89). The wider Qwen3 family dominates the WritingBench leaderboard (Qwen3-235B variants at 86-88%). In an independent clinical-note study (MIMIC-IV-Note summarization), Qwen3-32B was among the leading models for ABSTRACTIVE summarization (fluency/semantic adequacy) alongside DeepSeek-R1-70B and GPT-4o, while Gemma-3-27B led EXTRACTIVE summarization — suggesting Qwen3 favors generative, paraphrastic prose (good for drafting sections) and Gemma favors faithful extraction (good for not hallucinating). Strong reasoning (high GPQA/MATH in the Qwen3 technical report, arXiv 2505.09388) supports coherent argumentation and logical-gap detection for critique. Optional thinking mode aids structured peer-review-style critique (decomposing methods, identifying missing related work) but can be verbose. Quant note: runs well at Q4_K_M/Q5_K_M GGUF (Unsloth) or full BF16 on a 32GB+ GPU. Key gap for Labmate: Qwen3-32B base is TEXT-ONLY — it cannot ingest paper figures/charts/equation images, a real limitation when critiquing figure-heavy drafts (the VL line is a separate model). Chinese-origin training may slightly affect English idiom in formal academic register, though community reports rate its English technical prose highly.
benchmarks: WritingBench (10-pt, fine-tuned critic, >80% human agreement): Qwen3-32B-Instruct 8.64, Qwen3-32B-Base 6.89, DeepSeek-R1 8.55; Gemma 4 has NO published WritingBench score [uncertain]. General/reasoning (official sources): Gemma 4 26B A4B — MMLU Pro 82.6%, GPQA Diamond 82.3%, AIME 2026 88.3% (HuggingFace/Google blog; 31B dense slightly higher, exact 31B figures not individually published [uncertain]). Qwen3-32B — RULER avg 93.7 non-thinking / 91.0 thinking (Qwen3 tech report); GPQA/MATH strong but exact 32B GPQA Diamond not confirmed in retrieved sources [uncertain]. MIMIC-IV summarization study: Gemma-3-27B best at extractive, Qwen3-32B leading at abstractive. No EssayBench scores found for either model.
factual_accuracy: No SimpleQA or TruthfulQA scores were located for either Gemma 4 31B or Qwen3-32B specifically [uncertain]. Proxy signals: Gemma 4 26B A4B GPQA Diamond 82.3% (official) indicates strong graduate-science factual grounding; the MIMIC-IV study found Gemma-3-27B best at extractive summarization, implying lower confabulation when staying close to source — valuable for citation-faithful academic writing. Qwen3-32B's strength is abstractive (paraphrastic) generation, which historically carries marginally higher hallucination risk than extractive, so for Labmate's low-confabulation requirement Qwen3 critique outputs should be citation-checked. Both are mid-30B dense models without retrieval; neither should be trusted to invent citations. For a research assistant, pairing either with grounding (RAG over the actual paper text / Chroma) matters more than the raw model factuality delta.
inference_speed: Non-CUDA figures for the exact 31B/32B pair are sparse [uncertain]. Gemma 4 31B at Q4_K_M (~20GB) reports ~58-60 tok/s single-user decode on Ollama on high-end NVIDIA (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) and ~20+ tok/s on llama.cpp consumer GPU; CPU-only 1-8 tok/s. Gemma 4 additionally ships Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) speculative-decoding drafters (Transformers/MLX/vLLM/SGLang/Ollama) for further speedup — a real interactive-loop advantage. Apple Silicon: GGUF + MLX supported (Metal default-on). Qwen3-32B at Q4_K_M/Q5_K_M runs comparably (~30B dense, similar memory bandwidth bound); no MTP drafter. On Metal/ROCm both land in the same rough band at 4-bit; Gemma 4's MTP gives it an edge for latency-sensitive agentic turns. Specific ROCm/Metal tok/s for both at Q4 not separately benchmarked in retrieved sources.
multimodal_support: DECISIVE difference for paper reading. Gemma 4 31B-it: IMAGE input across all sizes (E2B/E4B also audio), with native Document/PDF parsing, chart comprehension, OCR (multilingual), screen/UI understanding, and variable-aspect-ratio image handling. It can read an academic paper page-as-image including embedded figures, plots, and rendered equations. Qwen/Qwen3-32B: TEXT-ONLY — the base 32B cannot accept images; Qwen's vision capability lives in the separate Qwen-VL line (not this model). For critiquing figure-heavy or equation-heavy drafts, only Gemma 4 can inspect the actual figures.
context_window: Gemma 4 31B: 256K nominal context (edge E2B/E4B are 128K), suited to passing whole papers or multi-paper literature-review sessions; effective-context/RULER for Gemma 4 not yet published [uncertain]. Qwen/Qwen3-32B: 32,768 native, extendable to 131,072 via YaRN (rope_scaling). Measured RULER (Qwen3 tech report): non-thinking avg 93.7 (98.4@4K down to 85.6@128K); thinking avg 91.0 (down to 83.5@128K) — strong, retrieval stays usable well past a single paper. A full paper (8-20K tokens) fits comfortably in both; a 32K+ literature-review session fits natively in Gemma 4 but requires YaRN on Qwen3 (which the Qwen team warns can degrade short-context quality if left always-on). Gemma 4's much larger native window is an advantage for multi-paper synthesis; Qwen3 has the published effective-context evidence Gemma 4 currently lacks.
non_cuda_support: Both have GGUF quants and run on non-CUDA backends. Gemma 4: official Unsloth GGUF/MLX support, llama.cpp (Metal default-on; build with -DGGML_CUDA=OFF for Apple, -DGGML_HIPBLAS=ON for ROCm/AMD), Ollama, LM Studio, MLX (Apple Silicon); NVIDIA also ships an NVFP4 vLLM checkpoint (CUDA). At Q4_K_M (~20GB) the 31B fits a single 32GB non-CUDA GPU (AMD RX 7900 XTX 24GB is tight at Q4 — better with the 26B A4B MoE; Apple M-series 36GB+ unified memory comfortable; AMD Radeon Pro W7800 32GB workable). Qwen3-32B: mature GGUF ecosystem (Unsloth, bartowski), llama.cpp ROCm/Metal/Vulkan, Ollama, MLX, LM Studio; ~32B dense at Q4_K_M ~19-20GB, same 32GB-GPU sweet spot. Build complexity is comparable (standard llama.cpp HIPBLAS/Metal flags). Both viable on a 32GB AMD/Apple host; Gemma 4 26B A4B MoE is the most non-CUDA-friendly option in either family for memory-constrained boxes.
over_refusal_risk: Qwen3-32B has measured over-refusal data: XSTest non-refusal 81.2, OK Test 84.0, OR-Bench 39.4 (per the 'Beyond Refusals' study) — the low OR-Bench figure indicates meaningful over-refusal on benign-but-sensitive prompts, a practical concern when an academic assistant discusses biosafety, dual-use, or controversial hypotheses. Qwen3Guard work shows the family is tunable toward lower refusal. Gemma 4 over-refusal (XSTest) not published for v4 [uncertain]; Gemma 3 historically had a moderate-to-conservative safety posture (community reported some over-refusal on edgy research topics). Neither is ideal for unrestricted dual-use discussion; for genuine biosafety/security research framing, expect occasional friction from both. No clear winner on hard data, but Qwen3's ~39% OR-Bench non-refusal is a documented weak spot.
ecosystem_toolchain: Both have broad day-one tooling. Gemma 4: official Google + HuggingFace launch with llama.cpp/GGUF, Ollama (gemma4:31b, Q4_K_M built in), MLX, vLLM (NVFP4 checkpoint by NVIDIA), Unsloth, LM Studio, plus MTP drafters and DiffusionGemma. Native function-calling and native system-role support. CRITICAL for Labmate: vLLM tool-call parser flag is 'gemma4' (NOT 'pythonic'/'gemma3'), with a dedicated tool_chat_template_gemma4.jinja and reasoning-parser gemma4 — matching Labmate's CLAUDE.md rule #6. High model-card quality. Qwen3-32B: extremely mature ecosystem (Apache-2.0), first-class vLLM with 'hermes' tool-call parser, Ollama, llama.cpp, MLX, Unsloth, SGLang, LM Studio; well-documented YaRN config; large community of quants. Both are agentic-ready; Gemma 4's tool surface is newer but officially supported, Qwen3's is battle-tested. Tie on maturity; Gemma 4 is the better fit for Labmate's already-gemma4-targeted vLLM config.
labmate_relevance: HIGH. This is Labmate's primary stated use case — writing academic prose, structuring arguments, generating paper sections (abstract/intro/related-work/methods/discussion), LaTeX output, and peer-review-style critique of drafts. Quality of argumentation, hedging calibration, citation fidelity, and the ability to read figure/equation-heavy papers all map directly to core daily tasks. This dimension should weigh heavily in the orchestrator-brain choice.
recommendation: Split decision favoring a model-switching strategy. For PURE-TEXT academic writing and critique (drafting sections, argument structuring, identifying logical gaps / missing related work, LaTeX prose), Qwen3-32B is the better-evidenced choice: it has the only published academic-writing benchmark (WritingBench 8.64, including the Academic & Engineering domain), leads abstractive summarization in independent testing, and has documented strong long-context RULER. Use it as the default writing/critique brain. For READING figure-heavy or equation-heavy papers — inspecting plots, tables, OCR of scanned PDFs, chart/diagram critique — Gemma 4 31B is the only option of the two, since Qwen3-32B is text-only; route any task that requires looking at the actual figures to Gemma 4. Gemma 4 also better matches Labmate's existing vLLM config (gemma4 tool-call parser, MTP speed, 256K native context for multi-paper synthesis) and is the designated orchestrator in CLAUDE.md. Tipping factors to settle the default brain: (1) run a private head-to-head on real draft critiques scored by a non-Gemma/non-Qwen judge (Labmate's testing rule), and (2) test LaTeX equation/table/figure-environment generation accuracy on both, since neither has published LaTeX-specific data. Pragmatic stance: keep Gemma 4 31B as orchestrator (multimodal paper reading + ecosystem fit), but delegate heavy pure-text drafting/critique to Qwen3-32B as a specialist worker — exactly the Gemma-orchestrator/Qwen-specialist split Labmate already plans.
